clue.text: Wish well, but give equivalent of beta minus

parts.note: beta is the Greek letter B
minus and less both mean with something taken away

explanation.surface: Someone offers good wishes while handing out a mark of beta minus, a slightly grudging grade.
explanation.walkthrough: Beta minus is read as B LESS, which runs together as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: To bless someone is to call down divine favour on them, a formal way of hoping things go well.

clue.text: Take over, given encouragement, with members being bent

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase for the adjective

parts.note: in cricket a bowler delivers an over of six balls
egged on means urged forward

explanation.surface: Someone takes control, cheered on by others, while the members bend the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take over' looks like assuming control, but it is the cricket sense: to bowl an over.
explanation.definitionFit: Members are limbs, and bow-legged describes legs curving outward at the knee.

clue.text: Being discriminating by gender, rejecting first son

definitions.note: a verb form, as in 'to be'

indicators.note: rejecting the first means the opening letter is thrown out

parts.note: sexist means discriminating on grounds of sex
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Gender bias that rejects a firstborn son, as in old inheritance rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Being as a verb form means living or having reality, which is the plain synonym here.

clue.text: Unseemly haste to get into action

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a disorderly rush or struggle
second meaning: of fighter pilots, to take off urgently

explanation.surface: An undignified rush to start doing something.
explanation.walkthrough: RAF fighter crews were ordered to scramble when told to get airborne at once.
explanation.definitionFit: A scramble is a chaotic rush, and as a verb it means urgently launching aircraft into action.

clue.text: I can still get excited enough to produce a little spark

indicators.note: excited things are stirred up and agitated, so the letters before it are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these three words are the fodder

explanation.surface: An ageing romantic insists they can still feel a spark of excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: Scintilla is Latin for a spark and in English means a tiny trace or particle of something.

clue.text: Tail-end of organized workers' rising

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the TUC is the Trades Union Congress, organised workers, plus the possessive S

explanation.surface: A union uprising seen from the rear, as if trade unionists were in revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: A scut is the short stubby tail of a rabbit, hare or deer, the animal's rear end.

clue.text: Imprecise notes in endless case

indicators.note: in means the first part goes inside the next
a case holds something, so the endless word encases the notes

parts.note: infinite means without end
two musical notes, D and E

explanation.surface: Vague notes lie in a case that drags on forever, perhaps a court file.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless case' reads like a lawsuit without end, but case is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Indefinite means not clearly defined or exact, so vague and lacking precision.

clue.text: One pays extra for this sort of truck

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone giving a gratuity
second meaning: a lorry whose body tilts to dump its load

explanation.surface: Someone pays a premium for a particular kind of lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipper leaves a tip on top of the bill, and a tipper truck tilts to unload.

clue.text: Sort of shoe, maybe, for end of evening?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, playful: a cobbler's last is a shoe-shaped thing
second meaning: the final moment before bed

explanation.surface: Choosing footwear for the close of a night out.
explanation.walkthrough: A last is the foot-shaped block a shoemaker builds a shoe on, so it is a shoe-like thing; 'maybe' flags the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Last thing at night is the idiom for just before going to bed.

clue.text: Prize the opposite of peace in our time?

indicators.note: in means the first part sits inside the next

parts.note: AD, Anno Domini, marks the present era
war is peace's antonym

explanation.surface: Echoes Chamberlain's 'peace in our time' promise, asking what its opposite would be.
explanation.walkthrough: Neville Chamberlain claimed 'peace for our time' in 1938, misquoted as 'peace in our time'; the phrase splits into parts here.
explanation.definitionFit: An award is a prize given in recognition of merit.

clue.text: Collection of sweet drinks

parts.note: a whip is a light dessert of whipped cream or egg whites
a round is a set of drinks bought for everyone in a group

explanation.surface: A pudding and a round at the pub, as if planning an evening out.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a sweet is a dessert course, and buying a round means paying for drinks for the whole group.
explanation.definitionFit: A whip-round is an informal gathering of money from colleagues or friends, for a gift or good cause.

clue.text: Infatuation with a Turkish officer

parts.note: pash is old British slang for a schoolgirl crush
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has fallen for a dashing officer of the Ottoman army.
explanation.definitionFit: A pasha was a high-ranking Ottoman military commander or provincial governor, the title placed after the name.

clue.text: Seal up sick note written by doctor

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing written by another sits beside it, here the second part following
something sick is out of sorts, so the word after it is disordered

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor signs a sick note and seals it in an envelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sick note' reads as a single thing, a medical certificate, but sick is the anagram signal working on note.
explanation.definitionFit: To entomb is to place in a tomb, sealing something or someone away inside.

clue.text: Moved camp

definitions.meaning: second meaning: theatrical, artificial in manner

explanation.walkthrough: 'Moved camp' reads like a tribe relocating; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Affected means emotionally stirred and also describes mannered, pretentious behaviour, both matching one word.

clue.text: Scoring method, of course, acceptable in extra match under way

indicators.note: in a down clue one thing under another is written after it

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: in means this part is placed inside the rest

parts.note: a replay is a match played again after a draw
OK means all right

explanation.surface: A golf scoring system is approved for an extra match already in progress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' means on a golf course. 'Under way' reads as 'in progress' but is two instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: Stroke play is the golf format in which total strokes taken are counted, rather than holes won.

clue.text: Terminate discussion of capital punishment

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in Parliament, to cut debate short by a timetable motion
second meaning: the French beheading machine

explanation.surface: Someone calls an end to a debate about the death penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: In the British Parliament a guillotine motion sets fixed times that cut debate on a bill short.
explanation.definitionFit: The parliamentary procedure borrows its name from the blade, and the machine was a means of execution.

clue.text: Is in better position to be inventive

indicators.note: in means the first word goes inside what follows

parts.note: to improve is to better one's position
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone well placed has more freedom to be creative.
explanation.definitionFit: To improvise is to create on the spot without preparation, an inventive response.

clue.text: Row either way in boat, if fitter

indicators.note: the letters wanted lie inside the following run of words
the run of letters can be read forwards or backwards and the same word appears both times

parts.note: concealed across the end of the first word and the following words

explanation.surface: A rowing crew wants anyone who is fitter to take either side of the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Forwards it spans boaT IF Fitter; backwards it sits in iF FITter. 'Row' looks like the oars but means a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiff is a minor quarrel, the sense of row that rhymes with cow.

clue.text: Warm glow here, if the girl is excited

indicators.note: something excited is agitated, so the preceding letters are stirred up

parts.note: the letters of these words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A girl's excitement shows as a warm glow on her face.
explanation.definitionFit: Firelight is the warm light given off by a hearth fire, the glow found by it.

clue.text: Violent, very masculine types held in check

indicators.note: held in means these go inside the next word

parts.note: to vet is to check thoroughly
he-men are men of exaggerated toughness

explanation.surface: Macho men are restrained before they turn violent.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehement means forceful, passionate and intense, close to violent in feeling.

clue.text: Stupid type given inside information

definitions.meaning: second meaning: slang for the low-down or a tip

explanation.surface: A fool gets let in on a secret tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is slang both for an idiot and for confidential details, as in getting the dope on someone.

clue.text: One operating still as a pirate

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an illegal distiller of liquor
second meaning: someone making unauthorised copies of recordings

explanation.surface: Someone keeps working quietly while living as a buccaneer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb meaning 'continuing', but it is the noun: a distilling apparatus.
explanation.definitionFit: Bootleggers made or smuggled illicit alcohol, and the word now also covers unlicensed copiers of music or films.

clue.text: After repair, hang a fine sort of rug

indicators.note: a repaired thing is put back together differently, so the following letters are rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Once mended, a good rug is ready to hang on the wall.
explanation.definitionFit: An Afghan is a hand-knotted rug from Afghanistan, or a knitted or crocheted blanket.

clue.text: Unharmed, protected by Hadrian's Wall?

parts.note: straight reading: escaping without penalty or injury
setter's reading: the people north of the Roman wall stayed free of Roman rule

explanation.walkthrough: Hadrian's Wall was built across northern England to keep out the tribes of what is now Scotland, so the phrase is read as free Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means getting away entirely unpunished or unhurt, scot originally being a tax.

clue.text: Point archbishop follows up in informal speech

indicators.note: in a down clue the archbishop follows by coming below the point

parts.note: S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: An archbishop raises a point in casual conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang is very informal vocabulary, words used in speech rather than formal writing.

clue.text: Simple book put right — lines entered the wrong way round

indicators.note: something that has entered goes inside the other part

parts.note: to heal is to make well, putting it right

indicators.note: the wrong way round means the letters run backwards

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the railway lines

explanation.surface: A book is corrected after lines of text were printed back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: A simple is an old word for a medicinal herb, so a simple book is a guide to herbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbal is a book describing plants and their medicinal uses, a catalogue of simples.

clue.text: Fetch ship, around noon

indicators.note: around means this word goes outside the next

parts.note: a brig is a two-masted sailing ship
N is short for noon

explanation.surface: Someone is told to collect a ship at about midday.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean going to collect something or someone and carrying it back here.

clue.text: Eat up, girl

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from the bottom

parts.note: to dine is to eat a meal

explanation.surface: A girl is told to finish her food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eat up' is a single phrase in the surface, but up is the turnaround signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid is a girl's name, as for the writer Enid Blyton.

clue.text: A contemptuous expression is silly

parts.note: taken as written
pish is an exclamation of scorn

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses an idea with a scornful sound, calling it silly.
explanation.definitionFit: Apish means like an ape: foolishly imitative or clownish in behaviour.

clue.text: Hanging on to endless underclothes is no good

parts.note: women's underwear
NG is the abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: Clinging to worn-out underwear is pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingering means staying on, slow to leave or fade, which is hanging on.

clue.text: Jealous author you had once cut

indicators.note: cut means the phrase before it is shortened by losing some of its middle

parts.note: Graham Greene, the English novelist

clue.text: Drunk is securely held

explanation.surface: A drunk is being held firmly, perhaps by the police.
